# Introduction

This workflow exports standard genomic tracks for downstream software and
retains structured R results for reproducibility. It uses the same synthetic
inputs as the [complete workflow](complete-workflow.html), with no external
downloads or persistent user-file overwrites. Package website:
<https://renscq.github.io/GeneTrackR/>.

# Prepare inputs and a temporary output directory

```{r inputs}
library(GeneTrackR)

demo_dir <- system.file("extdata", package = "GeneTrackR")
input_files <- c(
  annotation = file.path(demo_dir, "gtr_demo.genePredExt"),
  variants = file.path(demo_dir, "gtr_demo_variants.vcf"),
  phenotype = file.path(demo_dir, "gtr_demo_pheno.tsv"),
  signal = file.path(demo_dir, "gtr_demo_rnaseq_plus.bedgraph")
)
gp <- read_genepred(
  input_files[["annotation"]],
  format = "genePredExt",
  verbose = FALSE,
  progress = FALSE
)
vcf <- read_vcf(
  input_files[["variants"]],
  mode = "memory",
  verbose = FALSE,
  progress = FALSE
)
pheno <- read_pheno(
  input_files[["phenotype"]],
  verbose = FALSE,
  progress = FALSE
)
signal <- read_bwg(
  input_files[["signal"]],
  sample_names = "RNA_seq_plus",
  strand = "+",
  mode = "memory",
  verbose = FALSE
)
hap <- hap_gene_variant(
  vcf,
  annotation = gp,
  gene_id = "GeneA",
  genotype_mode = "string"
)
association <- plot_hap_pheno(
  hap,
  phenotype = pheno,
  traits = "protein_content",
  min_hap_samples = 3,
  test_method = "t.test",
  p_adjust = "BH",
  p_value_type = "adjusted",
  text_size = 10
)

output_dir <- tempfile("GeneTrackR-export-")
dir.create(output_dir)
```

For a production analysis, choose a deliberate output directory and keep input
files immutable. Record assembly, coordinate convention, signal units and
normalization, sample inclusion and all analysis parameters alongside outputs.

# Standard-format tracks

## Annotation

```{r annotation-output}
annotation_file <- file.path(output_dir, "annotation.genePredExt")
write_feature(
  gp,
  file = annotation_file,
  format = "genepredext",
  overwrite = TRUE
)
write_feature(
  gp,
  file = file.path(output_dir, "annotation.bed12"),
  format = "bed12",
  overwrite = TRUE
)
restored_annotation <- read_genepred(
  annotation_file,
  format = "genePredExt",
  verbose = FALSE,
  progress = FALSE
)
summary_feature(restored_annotation, level = "gene")
```

Writers apply the target-format coordinate convention. GTF/GFF3, BED and
GenePred represent different attributes and hierarchy information, so a
standard-format export should not be treated as a lossless copy of an entire
R workflow object. Use the function reference for supported formats and their
attribute/identifier policies; retain an RDS object when all metadata matter.

## Signal and VCF

```{r signal-and-variant-output}
signal_exports <- write_bwg(
  signal,
  outdir = output_dir,
  format = "bedgraph",
  overwrite = TRUE
)
variant_file <- file.path(output_dir, "variants.vcf")
write_vcf(vcf, file = variant_file, overwrite = TRUE)
restored_variants <- read_vcf(
  variant_file,
  mode = "memory",
  verbose = FALSE,
  progress = FALSE
)
summary_vcf(restored_variants)
file.copy(
  input_files[["variants"]],
  file.path(output_dir, "original-genotypes.vcf")
)
basename(signal_exports$file)
```

Signal export supports the existing bedGraph/WIG/BigWig layer. Consult
`?write_bwg` for chromosome-size and sample-splitting requirements, especially
for BigWig. Raw and normalized values are distinct outputs and should be
labelled with units and normalization parameters.

`write_vcf()` and `write_variant_track()` write eight site columns and a
minimal metadata header. The example also copies the original VCF for reuse
of the exact input text.

## Export a typed VCF with genotypes {#typed-vcf-export}

For a track created from a `CollapsedVCF`, use `as_vcf()` and the standard
writer. Use named samples to set their order. This path uses the header and
typed INFO and FORMAT data stored with the source object.

```{r typed-variant-output, eval=requireNamespace("VariantAnnotation", quietly=TRUE)}
source_vcf <- VariantAnnotation::readVcf(
  input_files[["variants"]],
  genome = NA_character_
)
adapted <- as_variant_track(source_vcf)
selected <- retrieve_vcf(
  adapted,
  chrom = "chr1",
  start = 12340000L,
  end = 12346000L,
  as = "VariantTrack",
  verbose = FALSE
)
typed_subset <- as_vcf(selected, samples = c("S02", "S01"))
typed_file <- file.path(output_dir, "selected-genotypes.vcf")
VariantAnnotation::writeVcf(typed_subset, typed_file)
restored_typed <- VariantAnnotation::readVcf(typed_file, genome = NA_character_)
head(VariantAnnotation::geno(restored_typed)$GT)
```

Keep the track's source metadata and row keys when filtering or saving it as
an RDS. Conversion rejects old native tracks, merged sources and edited site
or sample fields. The adapter also rejects absent `fileformat` declarations
and ambiguous empty ALT elements. Use `as_vcf(track, samples = character())` for a standard
sites-only object. The standard writer can update `fileDate`, round
floating-point FORMAT values and pad missing array entries. Save the typed
VCF object with `saveRDS()` when exact in-memory values are needed.

# Save statistical tables, figures and complete objects

```{r analysis-output}
utils::write.csv(
  association$summary,
  file = file.path(output_dir, "phenotype-summary.csv"),
  row.names = FALSE,
  na = "NA"
)
utils::write.csv(
  association$pvalue,
  file = file.path(output_dir, "pairwise-tests.csv"),
  row.names = FALSE,
  na = "NA"
)

figure_style <- ggplot2::theme(
  text = ggplot2::element_text(
    family = "Arial",
    colour = "black",
    face = "plain"
  )
)
classic_style <- ggplot2::theme_classic(base_family = "Arial") +
  figure_style +
  ggplot2::theme(axis.text = ggplot2::element_text(colour = "black"))
association$figure <- association$figure + classic_style
ggplot2::ggsave(
  filename = file.path(output_dir, "phenotype-comparison.png"),
  plot = association$figure,
  width = 8,
  height = 5,
  units = "in",
  dpi = 500,
  device = ragg::agg_png
)

bundle <- list(
  annotation = gp,
  variants = vcf,
  signal = signal,
  haplotypes = hap,
  phenotype = pheno,
  association = association,
  parameters = list(
    gene_id = "GeneA",
    genotype_mode = "string",
    min_hap_samples = 3,
    trait = "protein_content",
    test_method = "t.test",
    p_adjust = "BH"
  )
)
saveRDS(bundle, file.path(output_dir, "analysis.rds"))
restored <- readRDS(file.path(output_dir, "analysis.rds"))
restored$haplotypes$haplotypes
```

`plot_hap_variant()` and integrated-track functions return figures directly.
Phenotype and variant-effect functions return tables plus `$figure`;
`plot_ld_block()` normally returns LDTrack with `$figure`. Select the figure
component explicitly when calling `ggsave()`.

Report sample sizes, trait units, effect direction, adjustment method and
appropriate uncertainty, not only P values or significance symbols. For the
example's single trait, the six pairwise Welch t-tests use BH adjustment.
The complete object preserves interpretation context that is lost in a CSV
or image alone.

# Browser use and provenance {#browser-export}

For real IGV/UCSC-style browser inspection, use a reference/assembly matching
the exported coordinates and chromosome names. The demo coordinates describe
a synthetic model and are not a claim about a real reference genome. Load
annotation, signal and VCF tracks at the same interval and check strand,
sample labels and y-axis scale before comparing views.

GeneTrackR's integrated browser-like plot is generated in R, as demonstrated
in the [complete workflow](complete-workflow.html#integrated-browser). External
browser applications and network services are not required to execute these
vignettes.

```{r provenance}
provenance <- data.frame(
  role = names(input_files),
  input = basename(input_files),
  md5 = unname(tools::md5sum(input_files))
)
utils::write.csv(
  provenance,
  file = file.path(output_dir, "input-checksums.csv"),
  row.names = FALSE
)
capture.output(sessionInfo(), file = file.path(output_dir, "session-info.txt"))
list.files(output_dir)
```

Before sharing results, verify record counts, sample/ID alignment, missing
values, coordinate conventions, fields required by the target format and
read-back results. Keep original inputs and complete R objects. The
[annotation workflow](annotation.html) checks that direct transcript-level
CDS summaries match explicit segment aggregation, with one observation per
transcript and feature.

```{r session-info}
sessionInfo()
```
